name: Catalan

ancestors.notes: Central Catalan continues Old Catalan directly; the substrate/superstrate/adstrate layers (Iberian, Gothic, Andalusi Arabic, Occitan) are declared on the Old-Catalan node.

allophone_rules.notes: Word-final cluster simplification (Wheeler 2005 §10.4; Recasens 1993; Veny 1982 ch. 3): an ABSOLUTELY word-final stop is DELETED after a homorganic nasal or lateral — camp [ˈkam], sang [ˈsaŋ], quant [ˈkwan], molt [ˈmol]. An innovation of CENTRAL, NORTH-WESTERN and NORTHERN Catalan against the Old-Catalan core, which keeps the stop; VALENCIAN and BALEARIC keep it too (camp [ˈkamp], molt [ˈmolt]), and the 4catac expert transcriptions confirm the split on the one token that is diagnostic because a vowel follows — molt alta = Central/North-Western [ˈmol ˈalt-] vs Valencian/Balearic [ˈmolt ˈalt-]. The isogloss is therefore Central + North-Western (+ Northern) against Valencian + Balearic; it is NOT the Eastern/Western line. Overrides the core's conservative CA_CLUSTER_*_FINAL rule by id.

Central Catalan defaults an unmarked stressed ⟨o⟩ to open-mid [ɔ] and lists the close-[o] lexemes (the DCVB-cited word_exceptions gos/tot/dos/molt). 'corre' (córrer, close [ˈkorə]) was missing from that list, so this word-keyed rule pins ONLY its stressed vowel to close [o] and lets reduction and spirantisation run normally (DCVB s.v. córrer; Recasens 1996; the ca-009 arbitration).

stress.notes: Catalan accentuation per the Institut d'Estudis Catalans (IEC) norm (Gramàtica de la llengua catalana, ch. 3; Wheeler 2005 §3.1). A written accent (à è é í ò ó ú) always wins and marks the stressed vowel. Unmarked words are OXYTONE when they end in a consonant other than -s-preceded-by-a-vowel and other than -en/-in — including the consonant+s plurals (-ns, -rs, -ts, -nts, -ps …), which are oxytone because the plural preserves the stress of the singular (important → importants). A word ending in a falling DIPHTHONG (-ai -au -ei -eu -iu -oi -ou) is oxytone (remei [rəˈmɛj], correu [kuˈrɛw], avui [əˈβuj]) — the diphthong is one syllable, so the word does not end in a bare vowel. Unmarked words are PAROXYTONE when they end in a (single) vowel, in a vowel + -s (-as, -es, -is, -os, -us) or in -en/-in (semblen, parlin). The diaeresis ⟨ï ü⟩ marks hiatus/pronounced ⟨u⟩, NOT stress, so it is deliberately absent from marked_vowels (següent is [səˈɣwen], not [səˈɣwent] with stress on ⟨ü⟩). Proparoxytones always carry a written accent, so the unmarked default is paroxytone. The diphthongs list is the Catalan inventory of tautosyllabic vowel sequences (Wheeler 2005 §2.5; IEC grammar ch. 4): the falling diphthongs ⟨ai au ei eu iu oi ou ui⟩ and the rising ⟨ua ue uo ui⟩ after ⟨g/q⟩. Every other vowel sequence is HIATUS and counts as two syllables — te-ni-a, ve-ï-na, di-a — which is what puts the stress, and therefore the unstressed-vowel reduction, on the right vowel. CLITICS: cliticless_words lists the Catalan mots atons (IEC Gramatica de la llengua catalana ch. 3 and 6.2; Wheeler 2005 3.1) — definite articles el/la/els/les, the salat/literary lo/los, indefinite un/una/uns/unes, the article-preposition contractions al/als/del/dels/pel/pels, personal articles can/cal, the atonic prepositions a/de/en/amb/per/des, the conjunctions i/o/ni/que and atonic com, and the weak pronouns em/et/es/ens/us/el/la/els/les/li/hi/ho/ne and their reduced shapes. A clitic given a reduced lexical form in word_exceptions must not then be re-stressed (Recasens 1996).

notes: CENTRAL CATALAN (the Barcelona standard codified by the Institut d'Estudis Catalans). ⟨ca⟩ is the standard language and remains the code for 'Catalan'; what it is NOT is the parent of the other varieties — they inherit from ca-x-medieval (Old Catalan), so nothing declared here can leak into them. Everything in this file is a CENTRAL innovation against the Old-Catalan core: (1) stress-conditioned unstressed vowel reduction — unstressed /a e ɛ/ → [ə] and /o ɔ/ → [u], STRESSED vowels keeping full quality (gos [ˈɡos], dona [ˈdɔnə]) — keyed to the ⟨nucleus_unstressed⟩ slot, not to every nucleus (Wheeler 2005 §2.3); (2) betacism, ⟨v⟩ merged into /b/; (3) the fricative [ʒ] for ⟨j⟩ and ⟨g⟩ before a front vowel, where Old Catalan (and Valencian, and North-Western) has the affricate [dʒ]; (4) ⟨ix⟩ = [ʃ], the glide absorbed; (5) deletion of word-final ⟨-r⟩ (cantar [kənˈta]); and (6) deletion of an absolutely word-final stop in an ⟨-nt/-lt/-mp/-nc⟩ cluster (camp [ˈkam], molt [ˈmol]) — an innovation shared with North-Western and Northern but NOT with Valencian or Balearic. The stressed ⟨e⟩/⟨o⟩ close/open contrast is NOT recoverable from Catalan spelling (gos [ˈɡos] vs cos [ˈkɔs]); the default prior is OPEN-mid first, and the close-mid words are listed in word_exceptions.

sources.author: Wheeler, M. W.
sources.title: The Phonology of Catalan
sources.notes: The reference phonology of Catalan and the primary authority for this spec. Cited by SECTION, not page: §2.3 vowel systems and the unstressed reduction of the Eastern block (reduction is stress-conditioned; the Western block does not reduce); §2.5 the diphthong inventory; §3.1 stress and its orthographic marking; §5.1 the consonant inventory, ⟨c/g⟩ before a front vowel, ⟨x⟩ and word-final ⟨-ig⟩; §5.2 spirantization of /b d ɡ/ after a continuant and the pre-lateral gemination that blocks it; §5.3 final-obstruent devoicing and cross-word voicing assimilation; §10.2–§10.5 the post-lexical/phrase-level processes — final-rhotic loss, final-cluster simplification, nasal place assimilation and phrase-level lenition. Section numbers are given because the printed page numbers were not verified.

sources.author: Badia i Margarit, A. M.
sources.title: Gramàtica de la llengua catalana: descriptiva, normativa, diatòpica, diacrònica
sources.notes: Descriptive, normative, diatopic and diachronic grammar of Catalan; the cross-check used here for the consonant and vowel inventories, the stress rules and the dialect isoglosses. Pages not verified.

sources.author: Recasens, D.
sources.title: Fonètica i fonologia
sources.notes: Descriptive phonetics of Central Catalan: nasal place assimilation (labial before /p b m f/, velar before /k ɡ/, palato-alveolar before /ʃ ʒ tʃ dʒ ʎ/), spirantization and final-obstruent devoicing. Pages not verified.

sources.author: Recasens, D.
sources.title: Fonètica descriptiva del català: assaig de caracterització de la pronúncia del vocalisme i consonantisme del català al segle XX
sources.notes: The descriptive survey of Catalan vowels and consonants across the dialects: the Western block (Valencian, North-Western) does not reduce unstressed vowels; Balearic reduces ⟨a⟩/⟨e⟩ to [ə] but does NOT raise unstressed ⟨o⟩ to [u]; the North-Western word-final ⟨-a⟩ = [ɛ]. Pages not verified.

sources.author: Institut d'Estudis Catalans
sources.title: Gramàtica de la llengua catalana
sources.notes: The normative grammar. Ch. 3 (l'accent) is the source for the stress block: the written accent marks the stressed vowel and always wins; unmarked words ending in a vowel, a vowel+⟨-s⟩ or ⟨-en/-in⟩ are paroxytone and all other endings — including the consonant+⟨s⟩ plurals — are oxytone; the diaeresis ⟨ï ü⟩ marks hiatus, not stress. §6.2 and the 'mots àtons' list are the source for the clitic function words (articles, contractions, atonic prepositions/conjunctions and weak pronouns) that carry no stress and therefore reduce. Cited by chapter; pages not verified.

sources.author: Veny, J.
sources.title: Els parlars catalans: síntesi de dialectologia
sources.notes: The standard dialectology of Catalan and the source for the isoglosses this spec encodes per dialect: final ⟨-r⟩ retained in Valencian and deleted in the rest; final-cluster simplification after a nasal everywhere but after a lateral only in the Eastern block; Western [tʃ] for initial ⟨x⟩ and [jʃ] for ⟨ix⟩; the lleidatà final ⟨-a⟩ = [ɛ]. Pages not verified.

sources.author: Alcover, A. M. & Moll, F. de B.
sources.title: Diccionari català-valencià-balear
sources.notes: The dialectal dictionary of Catalan; it records the pronunciation of each headword per dialect and is the authority for the lexical stressed-mid-vowel entries in word_exceptions (gos, tot, dos, molt are close-mid [o]; cos, pont, font, tres are open-mid). Catalan spelling does not mark the ⟨e⟩/⟨o⟩ close/open contrast in unaccented syllables, so this contrast is lexical and can only be listed, not derived. Cited by headword; the dictionary is not paginated online.

sources.author: Bonet, E. & Lloret, M.-R.
sources.title: Fonologia catalana
sources.notes: Generative phonology of Catalan. Cited here by CHAPTER, not page: ch. 5 on syllable structure and hiatus resolution across a word boundary — which vowel elides, when a high vowel glides instead, and the clitic vowels that resist both. Used as the cross-check on Wheeler 2005 §10.1 for the cross-word vowel contact rules. Pages not verified.

sandhi_rules.name: cross-word-sibilant-degemination-s
sandhi_rules.notes:
External (cross-word) SIBILANT DEGEMINATION: where a word ends in the same sibilant that the next word begins with, the phonological phrase has a single sibilant, not a geminate — the coda one is deleted (Wheeler 2005, *The Phonology of Catalan*, §10.4 'consonant deletion in external sandhi'; Recasens 1993 §5). més són → [ˈme ˈson], dos savis → [ˈdo ˈsaβis], les sabates → [lə səˈβatəs], és seca → [ˈe ˈsɛkə].
Declared per DIALECT, not on the ca-x-medieval ancestor, because it is NOT pan-Catalan: Balearic assimilates and geminates instead of deleting, so ca-x-balear must not inherit this (see the note on ca-x-balear.json).
Scope, deliberately narrow on three axes, all measured. (1) IDENTICAL sibilants only: before a sibilant that DIFFERS in place or voicing the coda sibilant voices instead of deleting — petits juguen → [pəˈtidz ˈʒuɣən] (Wheeler 2005 §5.3), which CA_FINAL_TS_VOICING already handles. (2) SIBILANTS only: a cross-word stop or nasal geminate stays long in Catalan (tot tancat, constantment [kunstamˈmen]) and extending the deletion to stops or nasals measurably worsens every Catalan 4catac row. (3) VOICELESS sibilants only: word-final devoicing means no word surfaces with a final [z] or [ʒ] when these contexts are matched, so a z$ or ʒ$ rule could never fire. The consequence is that a /s # z/ boundary is currently left as a cross-word geminate (dos zeros → [ˈdoz ˈzɛɾus]) by CA_FINAL_S_VOICING: OUT OF SCOPE here, because collapsing it needs the deletion rules to see the post-voicing form, which the sandhi engine matches contexts against the ORIGINAL words to avoid. Pinned in tests/test_catalan_phonology.py::test_voiced_sibilant_boundary_is_a_known_gap.

sandhi_rules.name: cross-word-elision-final-schwa
sandhi_rules.notes:
VOWEL CONTACT across a word boundary, half one — ELISION of a word-final unstressed [ə]. Two vowels do not stand in hiatus across a boundary inside a phonological phrase; the weakest vowel goes, and [ə] is the weakest vowel the Eastern block has, so a word-final [ə] deletes before a vowel-initial word (Wheeler 2005, *The Phonology of Catalan*, §10.1 'vowel contact'; Bonet & Lloret 1998, *Fonologia catalana*, ch. 5 on hiatus resolution and clitic vowels.).
Engine output, verified: sobre el → [ˈsɔβɾ əl], començava a → [kuməˈnsaβ ə], troba entre → [ˈtɾɔβ ˈɛntɾə], petita aixella → [pəˈtit əˈʃɛʎə], tanta aigua → [ˈtant ˈajɣwə], cabana on → [kəˈβan ˈon]. The 4catac expert transcriptions write the same deletions.
Three conditions, all read off the gold. (1) NOT AFTER A GLIDE: the left context excludes [j w] before the [ə], because a [ə] closing a diphthong is the syllable's second mora and does not delete — feia anys is [ˈfɛjə ˈaɲʃ] in all four accents, not *[ˈfɛj ˈaɲʃ]. (2) NOT BEFORE AN UNSTRESSED HIGH VOWEL: an initial [i]/[u] resolves the hiatus by GLIDING instead (CA_HIATUS_GLIDE_I / _U), and when it does the preceding [ə] survives — beure un → [ˈbɛwɾə wn], pollastre i → [puˈʎastɾə j]. The right context therefore admits any STRESSED vowel but only the non-high unstressed ones, exactly the complement of what the glide rules take. (3) MINIMAL WORD. The context also guarantees the process cannot leave a word without a syllable: hiatus resolution in Catalan loses a vowel, never a word (Wheeler 2005, *The Phonology of Catalan*, §10.1 'vowel contact'; Bonet & Lloret 1998, *Fonologia catalana*, ch. 5 on hiatus resolution and clitic vowels. on clitic vowels and minimal-word behaviour). The left context requires a vowel EARLIER in the word than the [ə] being deleted, so a monovocalic clitic keeps its nucleus: la aigua is [lə ˈajɣwə], never *[l ˈajɣwə], and en la a i la e the article survives both times.
LIMIT, stated plainly: the 4catac annotators do write the proclitic que as bare [k] before a vowel (que ens [k ənz]) — Catalan spells that elision with an apostrophe, qu'ens. This rule does NOT produce it, because nothing in the IPA distinguishes a proclitic from any other monovocalic word, and generalising the deletion to every monovocalic word mutilates articles and conjunctions. Clitic elision is orthographic in Catalan and belongs to a caller that normalises the text, not here.

sandhi_rules.name: cross-word-elision-initial-unstressed-vowel
sandhi_rules.notes:
VOWEL CONTACT across a word boundary, half two — ELISION of the next word's initial UNSTRESSED vowel. Where the left word does not end in the elidable [ə], the hiatus is resolved on the other side (Wheeler 2005, *The Phonology of Catalan*, §10.1 'vowel contact'; Bonet & Lloret 1998, *Fonologia catalana*, ch. 5 on hiatus resolution and clitic vowels.).
Engine output, verified: va anar → [ˈba ˈna] (the 4catac gold writes the phrase as one word, [baˈna]; this library keeps the word boundary and the two forms are identical segment for segment), va experimentar → [ˈba kspəɾiməˈnta], he autoritzat → [ˈɛ wtuɾiˈdzat].
The two halves are mutually exclusive BY CONSTRUCTION, not by engine precedence: this rule's left context is the vowel set MINUS [ə], so a boundary whose left word ends in [ə] belongs to CA_ELIDE_FINAL_SCHWA and this rule cannot also fire on it. Exactly one vowel is lost per boundary.
High vowels are excluded from the right context for the same reason they are excluded from CA_ELIDE_FINAL_SCHWA's: an unstressed initial [i]/[u] GLIDES rather than deleting (CA_HIATUS_GLIDE_I / _U). Deletion and gliding partition the vowel space instead of competing for the boundary.
MINIMAL WORD. The context also guarantees the process cannot leave a word without a syllable: hiatus resolution in Catalan loses a vowel, never a word (Wheeler 2005, *The Phonology of Catalan*, §10.1 'vowel contact'; Bonet & Lloret 1998, *Fonologia catalana*, ch. 5 on hiatus resolution and clitic vowels. on clitic vowels and minimal-word behaviour). The lookahead requires ANOTHER vowel later in the same word, so a monovocalic word is never hollowed out: estava en oració keeps its preposition ([eˈstava en oɾasiˈo], not *[… n …]), que el keeps its article, and va a casa keeps its preposition [ˈba ə ˈkazə].
STRESS, and what the condition really does. An IPA stress mark precedes its vowel, so the unanchored right context ^[vowel] can only match a vowel with no mark on it. That is NOT the same as 'unstressed' in the prosodic sense: this engine writes no stress mark on an atonic monosyllable, so a clitic counts as unstressed here, which is right, while a stressed monosyllable that the engine leaves unmarked would also match. The condition is therefore 'carries no stress mark', and paga una is [ˈpaɣə wnə] rather than the gold's [ˈpaɣ ˈunə] precisely because the engine leaves una unmarked and the glide rule takes the boundary first.

sandhi_rules.name: cross-word-hiatus-glide-i
sandhi_rules.notes:
VOWEL CONTACT across a word boundary, the OTHER resolution — GLIDE FORMATION. A high vowel in hiatus need not delete: it loses its syllabicity and resyllabifies as an onset (Wheeler 2005, *The Phonology of Catalan*, §10.1 'vowel contact'; Bonet & Lloret 1998, *Fonologia catalana*, ch. 5 on hiatus resolution and clitic vowels.). A word-initial unstressed [i] after a vowel-final word surfaces as [j] — engine output, verified: pollastre i → [puˈʎastɾə j], de dellà i tanca → [də ðəˈʎa j ˈtaŋkə]. Note the preceding [ə] is KEPT, which is why CA_ELIDE_FINAL_SCHWA excludes unstressed high vowels from its right context.
No minimal-word guard here, deliberately, and this is the ONE place the constraint is relaxed: the bare conjunction ⟨i⟩ is exactly the word this rule is for, and all four 4catac accents write it as [j] between vowels (pollastre i, i ara). Gliding does not delete a segment — it changes its syllabicity — so the word is still pronounced; requiring it to keep a nucleus would contradict the expert gold and measurably worsens the Valencian and North-Western rows.

sandhi_rules.name: cross-word-hiatus-glide-u
sandhi_rules.notes:
VOWEL CONTACT across a word boundary — GLIDE FORMATION, the [u] half of CA_HIATUS_GLIDE_I. A word-initial unstressed [u] after a vowel-final word surfaces as [w] — engine output, verified: beure un → [ˈbɛwɾə wn], sobte un → [ˈsoptə wn] (Wheeler 2005, *The Phonology of Catalan*, §10.1 'vowel contact'; Bonet & Lloret 1998, *Fonologia catalana*, ch. 5 on hiatus resolution and clitic vowels.).
MINIMAL WORD. The context also guarantees the process cannot leave a word without a syllable: hiatus resolution in Catalan loses a vowel, never a word (Wheeler 2005, *The Phonology of Catalan*, §10.1 'vowel contact'; Bonet & Lloret 1998, *Fonologia catalana*, ch. 5 on hiatus resolution and clitic vowels. on clitic vowels and minimal-word behaviour). The lookahead requires a following segment, so a word that is nothing but [u] keeps its syllable: the conjunction ⟨o⟩, which the Eastern reduction realises as [u], stays syllabic in O Anna o Eva → [u ˈannə u ˈɛβə] instead of collapsing to a bare [w]. ⟨un⟩ has a consonant after the vowel and still glides, as the gold has it.
The MIRROR process on the LEFT side of the boundary — a word-final unstressed [i]/[u] gliding before a vowel-initial word (trobo adjectius [ˈtɾoβw ədʒəkˈtiws], deixo amor [ˈdeʃw əˈmor]) — is deliberately NOT declared: the Western accents write it with a non-syllabic diacritic on the original vowel quality ([ˈtɾoβo̯], [ˈðejʃo̯]) rather than as a plain glide, so one rule cannot state it for all four, and declaring the Eastern form measurably worsens the Valencian and North-Western rows.
